objective: Make the scope inference treat .claude/settings.local.json as repository-controlled when any tracked top-level entry is the same folder as .claude by identity, so a committed folder name that the file system folds onto .claude cannot steer a bare setup to local scope.
scope: Security finding (assignment-0mw8s8hov-9jat): packages/runtime/src/setup/scope.ts:208-226 lists the index only under the pathspec :(icase,literal).claude, which folds ASCII case only. A committed folder named '.claude.', '.claude ' (trailing space), a name with an HFS+ ignorable code point, or a Windows 8.3 short name such as CLAUDE~1 can fold onto the user's .claude on checkout; git ls-files then returns no entry, the identity loop added in 3869116 never runs, and installedScope infers local (scope.ts:258-259).

Fix as the reviewer proposed: list the tracked paths of the work tree (git ls-files --cached -z, limited to the work tree root's own entries), take the distinct first path components, and compare each component's lstat identity (dev and ino as bigint, as 3869116 does for files) with the identity of the .claude folder; a match means the repository controls .claude, so the local file is treated as tracked and inference stays at user. Keep the existing name and file-identity checks. Keep the cost bounded: stat each distinct top-level component once, with early exit on a match.

Add a regression test that fails without the change: a tracked top-level folder that is the same folder as .claude by identity (for example a symlinked or bind-style alias the test can create portably; if only a hard-linked directory would do and that is impossible, use a directory symlink committed as a tracked folder entry or another construction whose lstat identity equals .claude, and state which construction you used and why) never infers local; an ordinary repository with an untracked local file still infers local.

**Fix in `repositoryControl`**
- It now runs a single `git ls-files --cached -z` in the work tree root, replacing the `:(icase,literal)` pathspec call.
- The existing name, gitlink and file-identity checks run on the entries under `.claude`, filtered by lowercase prefix in code. Their results are unchanged.
- It then stats each distinct top-level component once, with early exit, and compares its dev:ino (bigint) with the `.claude` folder's.
- A match returns the reason `git tracks <component> as .claude`, so the scope stays user and the notice names the entry.
- I skip the component that is literally `.claude`. A normally committed `.claude/settings.json` has that component and shares the folder's identity, so without the skip it would block inference. A test caught this.
- The existing git-failure notice is unchanged.

**Test construction**
- A real repo tracks `.claude./settings.local.json`. `git ls-files -- :(icase,literal).claude` lists nothing for it, which the test asserts.
- Linux cannot fold names or hard-link folders. The test therefore spies `node:fs/promises` `lstat` (as `setup-files.test.ts` does) so the path `<repo>/.claude.` answers with the stats of `<repo>/.claude`, as a folding file system would. This keeps the test portable across platforms.
- A second new test confirms that unrelated tracked top-level entries (`src/`, `README.md`) with an untracked enabled local file still infer local.
- With the original `scope.ts` restored temporarily, the new identity test failed (65 pass, 1 fail). With the fix, all 66 pass.
